args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks — rolled back to v2.3.0 in all regions
args.summary:
At time of page, checkout-api was on v2.3.1 in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with healthy=false and error rate 18%.

Root cause: the latest deploy, v2.3.1, was unhealthy in production and had never been healthy there. (Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging.)

Actions taken:
1. Rolled back checkout-api to v2.3.0 — the most recent release with healthy status in production (v2.2.9 was also healthy but older).
2. The first rollback attempt was a partial failure: the rollout halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving us-east on v2.3.0 while us-west and eu-west remained on v2.3.1 (service version reported as "mixed").
3. Re-ran the rollback to v2.3.0; it completed in all three regions.

Current state: checkout-api is on v2.3.0 in us-east, us-west, and eu-west; healthy=true; error rate 0.2%.

Follow-up: investigate why the deploy process allowed an unhealthy/never-healthy version (v2.3.1) into all production regions, and why the initial rollback orchestration errored partway through. No change-manager approval was required for this rollback since v2.3.0 has already been healthy in production.

trace.final:
Done. Summary:

**Rollback**
- `checkout-api` was on **v2.3.1** in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), unhealthy, 18% error rate.
- Rolled back to **v2.3.0**, the most recent release marked healthy in production (v2.2.9 was older; v2.3.1 and v2.3.1-rc were unhealthy).
- The first rollback halted partway with an orchestrator error, leaving a mixed state (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1). I re-ran it and it completed in all regions.
- Verified current state: v2.3.0 everywhere, **healthy, 0.2% error rate**.

**Incident**
- Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2, for `checkout-api`, documenting the failure, the partial-failure/retry during rollback, the final healthy state, and follow-ups (how v2.3.1 reached full production without ever being healthy, and why the first rollout orchestration errored).
- The create call timed out client-side, so I checked `list_incidents` before retrying — the incident had in fact been created, so I did not re-submit it (avoiding a duplicate page to on-call).

No change-manager approval was needed: the rollback target v2.3.0 has already been healthy in production.
